observations.text: SP, due to a late power reduction and a mistimed configuration change in the break, did not establish the downwind parameters within the prescribed tolerances, carrying the A/C 380 feet above pattern altitude with airspeed 25 knots above the downwind target. Both values exceeded the +/- 300 feet and + 20 knots limits and were not recognized in time. The IP directed the corrections and flew part of the base turn in order to re-establish the briefed interval on the preceding A/C.

SP, due to loss of situational awareness of the aircraft's position in the pattern, did not fly the final segment on the prescribed altitude and AOA, descending 150 feet below the final altitude profile with the AOA 4 units off the on-speed indication. The deviations exceeded the - 100 feet and +/- 3 unit limits and were not corrected on the SP's initiative. The IP took the A/C and executed the go-around.

SP, due to an unstabilized power setting on base leg, did not control the approach airspeed within the prescribed tolerance, allowing the base leg speed to reach 20 knots above the target, at the code 1 limit. The excess speed was carried into the final turn and was recognized only after the IP's verbal prompt, with the correction applied with delay but without IP intervention on the controls.

SP, due to failure to monitor the aircraft state after the configuration change, did not hold the downwind altitude inside the prescribed band, climbing 300 feet above pattern altitude, at the code 1 limit. The deviation persisted past the abeam position and was corrected only after two verbal prompts from the IP. Recognition and correction of the error were delayed.

SP, due to an over-controlled roll input at the break point, did not hold the briefed break bank angle, reaching 13 degrees over the prescribed value and widening the downwind displacement. The deviation remained inside the +/- 15 degree limit and was recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention, with the briefed interval on the preceding A/C maintained.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, did not complete the landing configuration early enough to stabilize the final parameters, arriving on final 12 knots above the target airspeed and 150 feet above the altitude profile. Both deviations stayed inside the + 15 knots and + 200 feet limits and were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention.

SP flew the formation landing pattern within the desired standards, keeping break bank, downwind altitude and final airspeed inside the code 3 tolerances and preserving the briefed interval on the preceding A/C. However, the downwind altitude twice drifted to 140 feet high before being corrected, and the AOA on base leg oscillated up to 1.5 units off the on-speed indication. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter altitude and AOA control throughout the pattern is expected to improve.

SP flew the formation landing pattern with negligible deviations, holding break bank within 3 degrees of the briefed value, downwind and final altitudes within 30 feet and approach airspeeds within 3 knots of the targets. AOA was kept within half a unit of the on-speed indication from downwind through final, and the briefed interval on the preceding A/C was maintained without any IP input. Pattern sequencing and radio calls were accurate and rapid throughout the recovery. Above end of block MIF achieved.
